name: LME49721
type: Rail-to-rail I/O audio dual, 2.2–5.5 V, CMOS-type input
tagline: Rare audio-grade rail-to-rail dual for 5 V rails: 4 nV/√Hz, 0.00008% THD+N. A Japanese low-voltage headphone-amp pick.

lineage.note: Part of the LME audio line (LME49720, LME49710). Datasheet originated September 2007; National copy dated October 2007.
Acquired National in 2011. Reissued the datasheet in TI format as SNAS371C (April 2013). Still sold.

part_numbers.note: SOIC-8 tube, lead-free. Probably active; no explicit TI lifecycle flag seen.
SOIC-8 tape and reel, lead-free. Active per Octopart.
Legacy National non-NOPB codes (MA tube, MAX reel). Status unconfirmed.

reputation.summary: A standard pick among Japanese builders of low-voltage and portable headphone amps. nabe's blog recommends it with the AD8656 after low-voltage tests; a zigsow review calls it "really excellent"; Akizuki sells it as a full-swing HiFi op-amp. Praise comes mostly from these Japanese hobbyist sources, not Western forums.
typical_uses: Low-voltage single-supply paths needing rail-to-rail swing
caveats: 5.5 V total supply limit: ±12 V or ±15 V NE5532/OPA2134 sockets will destroy it.
Output current only about ±9.7 mA, limiting direct drive of low-impedance headphones.
SOIC-8 only; DIP-8 sockets need an adapter.
Praise rests on a small number of Japanese hobbyist sources.

counterfeit_notes: No LME49721-specific counterfeit reports found. Only SOIC-8 (MA) codes exist, so a native DIP-8 'LME49721' is an adapter board or suspect. Buy from authorized distributors (TI, DigiKey, Mouser).

revision_history.changes: Initial release. TI header gives September 2007 origination; the National copy is dated October 2007.
Reported date of a copy printed SNAS371B; changes not recorded. Some National copies carry a 2010 copyright.
Changed the National data sheet layout to TI format.

revision_chains.note: Rev B date from one distributor copy (probable). National pages carry document code 202049; rev A not found.

open_questions: Date and change list of SNAS371A; confirm SNAS371B date (21 April 2010) against the PDF.
Which revision each mirror (Octopart, alldatasheet 538445/538446/2194639, datasheet4u, radiolocman) actually holds.
Any PCN or fab/die transfer after the TI acquisition? Check TI PCN listings.
Lifecycle status of legacy LME49721MA / MAX codes, and an explicit TI flag for LME49721MA/NOPB.
THD+N test conditions, and whether quiescent current is per amplifier or total.

claims_confirmed: Current TI datasheet is SNAS371C, 'September 2007 – revised April 2013' (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/lme49721.pdf).
Rev C (04/04/13) moved the National layout to TI format (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/snas371c/snas371c.pdf).
A National datasheet copy dated October 2007 exists (https://www.pken.net/ish_mm/datasheet/ns/lme49721.pdf).
Key specs as listed, from https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/lme49721.pdf and https://datasheet.octopart.com/LME49721MA/NOPB-National-Semiconductor-datasheet-9809305.pdf.
TI part-details pages exist for both /NOPB codes (https://www.ti.com/product/LME49721/part-details/LME49721MA/NOPB).
AN-1767 LME49721 Evaluation Board is TI document SNAA051 Rev A (https://www.ti.com/lit/pdf/snaa051).
corrections: Channel count corrected from 0 to 2 for all part numbers.
Added /NOPB ordering codes: MAX/NOPB active per Octopart, MA/NOPB probably active.
LME49721MA and LME49721MAX reclassified as legacy National codes with unknown status.
Bias current set to confirmed 40 fA typ; ±9.7 mA output current added.
No silicon changes or revision hazards found.
